title: Operator policy: coordinated upgrades; in-place client updater is the sole cross-version tool compatibility requirement

conditions.description: Operator explicitly states: 'The ONLY tool that needs to always work is the one to trigger in-place update', following the decision that we control all clients and will update them. Record as project-wide engineering/release policy, reconcile existing specs/reviews and remove ordinary tool mixed-version interoperability requirements; fail closed with clear upgrade guidance as appropriate. Preserve a minimal stable authenticated update_client control path across supported installed client versions and newer server releases, independent of normal protocol mismatch gates and optional diagnostics where feasible; verify real mixed-version update trigger, verified artifact selection/integrity, correct target, reconnect and failure/rollback semantics. Identify any existing task covering this and extend it rather than duplicating; if absent create focused task. Keep normal matched-version semantics, independent review, deployment qualification and security boundaries. This policy does not itself authorize executing a live update or restarting the local client. Return canonical policy location and task IDs.
conditions.evidence: Binding project-wide coordinated-upgrade policy persisted in canonical 1.0 completion epic jarvis-1-0-robustness-and-ergonomics-completion-20261127 v10 seq20913; normal tools matched-version, sole stable authenticated cross-version update trigger, no security/qualification waiver or live restart. Existing updater task client-self-update-arbitrary-executable-name-20261122 expanded P0 seq20910 and assigned W1 Ready seq20911, scope includes stable route, archived peers, actual device/artifact/rollback/reconnect evidence and truthful bootstrapping boundaries. W6 spec adoption seq20909 eliminates mixed-peer-only work; no duplicate implementation. Shared route changes require explicit lease reconciliation.
